Report_ID: KOOS knee-related quality of life (QOL), change at 6 months
Title: Six-week high-intensity exercise program for middle-aged patients with knee osteoarthritis: a randomized controlled trial [ISRCTN20244858]
Author: Thorstensson CA, Roos EM, Petersson IF, Ekdahl C
Comment: Table 2 reports mean change with 95% CIs, not standard deviations; no SDs of change scores are reported, so SMD cannot be computed directly from the paper's own numbers. The longest follow-up in this trial is 6 months (no 12-month assessment), which is within the plan's <=12-month longer-term window. Per-group analysed N = 28 each ("Twenty-eight patients in each group were available for follow-up"); randomized Ns were 30 and 31.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Exercise group (six-week supervised high-intensity exercise, twice weekly 1-hour sessions at >=60% HRmax plus daily home exercises)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); treatment SD derived from its reported mean CI; control SD derived from its reported mean CI
Participant type: Middle-aged adults (36-65 years) with symptomatic and definite radiographic knee osteoarthritis (Kellgren & Lawrence grade III or more)
Recruitment source: Patients referred for radiographic examination due to long-standing knee pain at Halmstad County Hospital and area general practitioners, Sweden (Oct 1998 - Oct 2001)
Outcome measurement: Mean change in KOOS QOL subscale score from baseline to 6-month follow-up (0-100, worst to best; positive = improvement), between-group comparison with Mann-Whitney U-test
Outcome variable: KOOS knee-related quality of life (QOL), change at 6 months
outcome_units: KOOS points (0-100 scale, 0 = extreme problems, 100 = no problems)

Report_ID: SF-36 Physical Health score (week 14, 6 weeks post-intervention) — RT vs control
Title: Effects of home-based resistance training and neuromuscular electrical stimulation in knee osteoarthritis: a randomized controlled trial
Author: Bruce-Brand et al.
Comment: No between-group inferential statistic, effect size or CI is reported for SF-36; only a narrative statement of "no between-group differences". Group Ns in Table 2 are as-randomised (RT n=10, Control n=6) although only 26/41 participants overall were available at week 14, so per-timepoint analysed Ns may be smaller. M_diff not computed because the design is a 3-arm mixed-design repeated-measures ANOVA. Note: follow-up is 6 weeks post-intervention (week 14), not 12 months.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Home-based resistance training (RT)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: single-centre hospital-based trial with home-based interventions
Participant type: Patients aged 55–75 years with symptomatic moderate to severe knee osteoarthritis
Recruitment source: Cappagh National Orthopaedic Hospital arthroscopy database and knee arthroplasty waiting list, Greater Dublin area
Outcome measurement: Self-reported questionnaire, aggregate physical health score (0–100, higher = better health)
Outcome variable: SF-36 Physical Health score (week 14, 6 weeks post-intervention) — RT vs control
additional_group_ns: NMES arm not used in this row: NMES (n=10), SF-36 Physical Health week 14 = 47.60 ± 10.73
outcome_units: SF-36 physical health aggregate score points

Report_ID: Knee-related quality of life (KOOS QoL) at 1 year — strength exercise vs usual care
Title: The efficacy of strength or aerobic exercise on quality of life and knee function in patients with knee osteoarthritis. A multi-arm randomized controlled trial with 1-year follow-up
Author: Øiestad et al.
Comment: M_diff is the paper's model-based adjusted mean difference with sign convention exercise minus usual care (positive favours exercise); mixed linear model adjusted for baseline KOOS QoL. SE_diff derived from the reported 95% CI as (14.0 - (-0.9))/3.92. Group means/SDs in Table 2 are unadjusted descriptives. Three-arm trial: the usual-care arm is shared with the aerobic-exercise row.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Strength exercise (12 weeks, physiotherapist-supervised)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults aged 35-70 with symptomatic and radiographic (Kellgren-Lawrence 2-3) knee osteoarthritis
Recruitment source: Primary care, orthopedic departments at three hospitals in greater Oslo, and newspaper advertisements
Outcome measurement: Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (KOOS), QoL subscale, self-reported
Outcome variable: Knee-related quality of life (KOOS QoL) at 1 year — strength exercise vs usual care
additional_group_ns: Third arm not used in this row: aerobic exercise (stationary cycling), n=39 with 1-year KOOS QoL data (extracted as a separate row)

Report_ID: KOOS quality of life (0-100) at 3-month follow-up — land-based exercise vs control
Title: A randomized controlled trial of aquatic and land-based exercise in patients with knee osteoarthritis
Author: Lund H, Weile U, Christensen R, Rostock B, Downey A, Bartels EM, Danneskiold-Samsøe B, Bliddal H
Comment: Means are ANCOVA-adjusted means reported with standard ERRORS (SE), not SDs. SE_diff derived from the reported 95% CI of the group mean difference as (8.7 - (-5.3))/3.92 = 3.571; the paper states CIs for these scores are based on the t-distribution, so this is approximate. Follow-up is 3 months after exercise cessation, not 12 months.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Land-based exercise (8 weeks, 2 sessions/week)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); ANOVA: missing F-value or group sizes
Study Environment: Hospital physiotherapy department / clinical motor function laboratory
Participant type: Adults with primary knee osteoarthritis (ACR criteria), mean age 68 years, 62/79 women
Recruitment source: Outpatient clinic, general practitioners, and local newspaper advertising
Outcome measurement: Normalized KOOS quality of life subscale score (100 = no symptoms, 0 = extreme symptoms); higher = better
Outcome variable: KOOS quality of life (0-100) at 3-month follow-up — land-based exercise vs control
additional_group_ns: Aquatic exercise arm (n = 27) reported in the same table but not used for this treatment-vs-control row (extracted separately)

Report_ID: Health-related quality of life (MACTAR) at 6-month post-intervention follow-up
Title: Clinical Effectiveness of a Rehabilitation Program Integrating Exercise, Self-Management, and Active Coping Strategies for Chronic Knee Pain: A Cluster Randomized Trial
Author: Hurley MV, Walsh NE, Mitchell HL, Pimm TJ, Patel A, Williamson E, Jones RH, Dieppe PA, Reeves BC
Comment: SE_diff derived from the reported 95% CI of the between-group difference: (4.04 - 0.36)/3.92 = 0.9388. Group values in Table 2 are model-estimated means with 95% CIs (no SDs reported), so no SD could be extracted. The paper's own standardized effect size is printed as -0.27 (-0.50, -0.04); its sign convention is inverted relative to the direction of benefit for higher-is-better scales (cf. WOMAC-func difference -3.33 with effect size +0.29), so the magnitude 0.27 is recorded as favouring rehabilitation. Timepoint is 6 months after completing the intervention (the only post-intervention follow-up reported; no 12-month assessment exists). EQ-5D (difference -0.01, 95% CI -0.08, 0.05; P = 0.709) measures the same construct in the same comparison and was not recorded separately to avoid double counting.
Design Type: pragmatic single-blind cluster randomized controlled trial
domain: musculoskeletal rehabilitation / chronic knee pain (knee osteoarthritis)
Study Environment: Rehabilitation Research Unit and Physiotherapy Out-patient Department, Dulwich Community Hospital
Participant type: Adults age >50 years with chronic knee pain (>6 months) recruited from 54 inner-city primary care practices
Recruitment source: Primary care practice databases, South East London, UK
Outcome measurement: Estimated mean MACTAR score at 6 months from multilevel model adjusting for baseline values and intracluster correlation; higher scores indicate better health status
Outcome variable: Health-related quality of life (MACTAR) at 6-month post-intervention follow-up
additional_group_ns: Randomized: usual care n=140, Indiv-rehab n=146, Grp-rehab n=132 (total 418); the two rehabilitation arms are combined in this analysis as reported by the paper
